summary:
We received your card showing a horrible snake doing unspeakable things, and of course it delighted us. Thank you. Certainly it is much nicer than the fac­ tory-made ones showing Santa throwing handfuls of heroin and cocaine to little children. We get a lot of those. (“Snow,” it’s called in the subculture.) Mildred, your letter of November 20 did contain some sad news, and you have our understanding and sympathy and hopes ... Tessa, as I may have men­ tioned, turned out to be Rh negative, and I did not have the exact same type. So we abandoned our plans of last year and stuck close to the hospital here. Now, of course, we are free to travel north, but we are wondering if.we would 
freeze to death there. Which is better, that, or to stay here and die of hunger, since 99% of all our goods are trucked in and the trucks will soon be in grave­ yards all over the world? Nothing grows here except fields of Coca Cola. You can’t see them, though, because of the smog. But they’re there. Would a pack­ age deal interest you? 

Was Bill’s oldest girl who had a baby on November 17th the oldest of the girls I met at the Westercon? They were all such lovely girls and reminded me of the three stepgirls I lost in a previous marriage whom my exwife won’t even let write to me now, let alone visit. The two eldest are married, but I can t even get their addresses so I can write them. Life can be mean, sometimes. 

The Nebula Banquet will cost $25 and I’m not sure we can afford to go to it. Despite...
